newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PNG/Bougainville peace talks to start in NZ.
newsitem.headline: PNG/Bougainville peace talks to start in NZ.

text.p: Talks aimed at ending the secessionist war on Papua New Guinea's Bougainville Island will begin this weekend in New Zealand, Foreign Minister Don McKinnon said on Wednesday.

McKinnon said in a statement that the meeting would bring together senior members of the PNG-backed Bougainville transitional government, the Bougainville interim government and its military wing, the Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRA).
The talks were due to begin at the Burnham army camp near the South Island city of Christchurch this weekend, he added.

"This is a step along the path towards settlement of their differences with the Papua New Guinea government. It should not be assumed there is a quick fix solution to the situation in Bougainville," McKinnon said.
The conflict on the resource-rich island, 800 kilometres (500 miles) northeast of Port Moresby, has claimed thousands of lives and dates back more than eight years.

In March, PNG was plunged into its worst political crisis since independence when the army revolted over Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan's hiring of African mercenaries to end the Bougainville rebellion.
Chan lost his seat in nationalist elections on Tuesday, and predicted his career in politics was over. He blamed the US$36-million mercenary plan for his downfall.
McKinnon said New Zealand offered to host the meeting after approaches from the Bougainville groups and discussions with the Papua New Guinea government.
He noted that the New Zealand government would not take part in the talks, however.
"It is the express wish of the Bougainvilleans to gather for private discussions on how to bring about peace and reconstruction," the minister told a Wellington news conference.
"Since the all-Bougainville talks in Cairns (Australia) in late 1995, we have become increasingly concerned at the pace of progress towards peace and reconstruction on Bougainville.
"I have been encouraging all parties to this dispute to resolve their differences, making it clear that New Zealand is willing to assist this process in whatever way we can," he said.
There has been diplomatic speculation for several weeks that a new round of peace talks was imminent and would be held in either New Zealand or Australia.
Port Moresby unveiled a fresh outline peace initiative in late May.
Many past rounds of peace talks and military offensives have failed to resolve the conflict.
